memory_update.text: Add FORM as a high-priority HBM second-order candidate: probe-card demand is directly linked to HBM DRAM testing and generative-AI memory ramps.
Add TER as a high-priority HBM test candidate: Magnum 7H and annual-report language provide direct evidence of AI-driven HBM/DRAM memory-test exposure.
Add AMKR as an advanced-packaging/OSAT candidate: direct HBM packaging relevance is plausible, but revenue attribution to AI/HBM still needs stronger customer-level evidence.
Add CAMT as an inspection/metrology candidate for HBM, chiplets, memory, and advanced packaging; evidence is company-disclosed but revenue segmentation needs verification.
Add ONTO as a process-control/metrology candidate for HBM/GPU AI packages; direct tool relevance is clear, but customer qualification evidence should be checked.
For the AI accelerators + HBM node, include test, probe-card, metrology, and advanced-packaging suppliers as first-class chokepoint-adjacent mappings, not only GPU, memory, and foundry names.

Need a follow-up pass on materials and consumables for HBM/advanced packaging, including temporary bonding, electroplating chemistry, substrates/interposers, thermal interface materials, and ultra-clean process inputs.

summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the AI accelerator + HBM node toward less obvious second-order chokepoint exposures. The most relevant additions are not only GPU/ASIC and memory vendors, but also wafer probe cards, HBM memory testers, advanced packaging/test capacity, and inspection/metrology suppliers needed to raise HBM and 2.5D/3D package yields. All five candidates screened above USD 1B market cap using current web finance data, but inclusion is research-priority only, not a trading recommendation.
